question: At byte-identical inputs, do the MPS and native Metal SSB paths stay inside a strict float32/complex64 bound of an independent double-precision evaluation, does the frozen fit trajectory survive enabling the batched pair draw, and how much of the 200-trial fit budget is load-bearing?

inputs.note: 512x512 x 192x192 uint16 real acquisition; the export proves every selected value against an independent h5py read (0 mismatches in 2,342,780,928 values)
the executable QuantEM/Python reference; defaults to optuna_batch_size = 2

parameters.brightfield_policy: documented full disk minus one hardware dead pixel (78, 74): 8937 logical, 2464 aperture-active
parameters.precision: exact uint16 raw counts, float32 real, complex64 complex, no binning, no crop, no fast-math path, no CPU fallback in any measured path
parameters.gate_rule: min(absolute float32 bound, 2x the measured single-precision floor of the identical formula evaluated with SciPy pocketfft)

fit_gate.pin_basis: sha256 over (float32 point, float64 loss, stage) of all 220 recorded evaluations

outcomes.metal: passes every gated metric at 128x128 and 512x512; best object relL2 5.618e-07
outcomes.mps: deterministic failures at 512x512 (object relL2 4.317e-06 against a 2.196e-06 bound; mps-vs-metal 4.179e-06) and at one recorded 128x128 setting (loss 2.875e-07 against a 2.24e-07 bound)
outcomes.mps_root_cause: named line: the per-BF weighting construction. Rebuilding the probe term in-kernel at identical accumulation moves the 512x512 object relL2 from 4.3173e-06 to 3.8184e-06 (15% of the excess over the 1.0981e-06 floor); accumulation order/depth (<=0.4% over 18-140 groups, Kahan compensation 0.07%, bit-identical under math_mode fast) and the trig spelling/FMA mode and the forward transform are all excluded by measurement. The object fix provably cannot move a fit: the fit never builds the object kernel, and a patched 200-trial reference fit reproduces digest 227cb1f4 bit for bit.
outcomes.fit_trajectory: deterministic across processes (sha256 74cc777234a5ec107647ba0be60580c9abb58d0eca1ca3e6fd6b2cbeab93d72b); production optimize reproduces it exactly; the batched pair draw moves the optimum and is not the production path
outcomes.recorded_cached_vs_streamed_defect: closed in-tree by the ssb_ifft512_nyquist_correction; the cached half-plane path was the wrong one
outcomes.f1_attribution: one lever per process at 512x512 setting #0: per-BF weighting construction is the line (pk-inline 3.8184e-06, -11.6%); accumulation re-order/chunk <=0.4%; Kahan 0.07%; metal::fast::sincos vs metal::sincos bitwise identical over 18,302,976 real chi samples; SciPy float32 and float64 forward transforms leave the object unchanged; error field diffuse (median 1.26e-05, max 3.96e-05). The MPS loss passes structurally, not by luck: it is a phase-moment computation, agreeing with metal:cached to 0-2.0 float32 ulp on all 9 gated rows.
outcomes.trial_budget: 512x512 / 8937 BF / seed 42, Metal production path, no arithmetic change: tpe50 = tpe100 = tpe200 to the last bit (optimum 52.871296844577195, 52.878826420320394, 0.0021567655543952434; loss 0.096058391034603119); trials 50-200 buy exactly 0.0 (150 trials, 12.1 s of 20.4 s); 25 trials is not enough (1.17e-03 worse); a second Nelder-Mead from the recorded optimum buys 1.532e-03 more than the whole search bought, so NM termination, not the trial budget, is the binding constraint. Forward/reverse traces bit-identical; the tpe200 trace reproduces the recorded fit bit for bit.
outcomes.gate_harness: the --metal-only exit status is the Metal acceptance signal and the run now says so in its own output: 'NOTE: --metal-only - the MPS implementation is NOT measured in this run' plus a final 'PASS: strict float32 parity (Metal pairs only, MPS not measured - not a full-gate pass)'. Verified end to end: 185 gated rows ok, 0 FAIL, 0 MPS rows, exit 0. Documented pytest command needs QUANTEM_SSB_PARITY_REPORT=parity-runs/gate-fast.json when not re-measuring (finding F10).
outcomes.harness_reconciliation: 3.4x is the executed-term count, not the harness: 2,464 against 8,937 executed BF terms (3.627x) versus a measured per-eval ratio 0.073618 -> 0.267578 s (3.635x) at an identical timer, source buffer, column order and full cache. Production is the disk-matched app configuration (SSBExplorer.swift:95/347/440); the user's 200-trial + NM protocol costs 58.6-64.6 s single run at load 1.3-2.0, not 30 s.
outcomes.production_fit_identity: On the production configuration (8,937 executed terms, seed 42, start (0,50,0)) 25 trials + NM is NOT bit-identical to 200 trials + NM: tpe25 loss 0.15314710140228271 and optimum (6.1600740257507347, 0.37580517960110538, 1.650074148576167) against tpe200 loss 0.15314708650112152 and (5.8845526481201356, 0.46141110440991562, 1.3530133901569708), a 9.7e-08 relative loss difference with c10 moving 4.7% and phi12 0.30 rad. The 25-trial TPE prefix is bitwise identical (0/25 differ) and tpe200 reproduces across processes bit for bit; NM-only from the tpe200 optimum moves again to loss 0.15314705669879913, so the optimum is NM-termination-limited inside a flat valley.
outcomes.mps_fit_blocker: MPS sees the same production objective (loss at the Metal app-config optimum agrees to 3.795e-06 relative) but session.fit raises 'Exact 512 pair pack of 512 BF planes exceeds the 320-plane storage class' on this Apple M5, so the 25-vs-200 and NM-warm identity checks could not be run on MPS (F11).
